conditional_prerequisites.reason: The token-identity rejection remains immutable; v23 uses only the retained speed signal.
The fused kernel must preserve the frozen same-weights capability gates before it may consume an approximate model.
V10 remains rejected; v23 tests a new composition rather than rewriting that outcome.

hypothesis: The activation-calibrated v10 compute image makes all 6.734B formerly-Q8 weights eligible for the quality-adjudicated native-x4 Q4_K kernel. Combining fewer streamed bytes with shared four-row Q4 decode should produce a material end-to-end MTP3 gain beyond either retained signal alone, while the frozen calibration can preserve control-level capability.
scientific_boundary: This is a predeclared systems-composition test of two independently retained signals. It is not presumed multiplicative, novel, semi-lossless, or a breakthrough.

stop_rules: Do not execute v23 unless v22 terminates with every frozen quality gate passed.
Do not reinterpret the v10 or v21 terminal rejections.
Reject before serving if any artifact, backend, graph, stability, or frequency gate fails.
Run all quick-quality denominators after a valid noncollapsed artifact even if graph, serving, or another quick-quality gate fails.
Do not run MMLU-64 unless every prior performance and quick-quality gate passes.
Do not tune calibration, prompts, thresholds, tensor selection, artifact bytes, or kernel arithmetic after observing v23 results.
Preserve terminal negative receipts and remove surplus regenerated candidates after hashing.
promotion_boundary: A pass would establish a reproducible quality-qualified Qwen3.8-27B CPU composition with at least a 1.20x MTP3 accepted-throughput gain over the stock system on four Milan cores. It would not satisfy the 2.75 tok/s conventional-decode breakthrough gate, establish final-node or energy scaling, reach 100 tok/s, or support novelty or scientific-breakthrough claims.
